_note: Every step names a control TYPE as well as a name or AutomationId, and the resolver additionally requires the UIA pattern the verb needs. This is not decoration: five elements in this app are named 'Settings' (a Window, a TitleBar, two Texts and the Button), and a name-only FindFirst returns the Window, which carries no InvokePattern. Steps that resolve to zero or to more than one element are errors, never a silent first-match.
_note_f013: Since the F-013 shell fold (2026-08-21), Games/Settings/History/Diagnostics/Plugins/About are PAGES of one non-modal ShellWindow whose title tracks the active page. The routes below survive because the shell answers to the same Window names the six windows carried (the title IS the destination noun), and Settings' inner rail keeps its SettingsNav name. Only About's captured name changed: the About WINDOW was allowed the product name, the shell page is titled plain 'About'. close-window on a destination name now closes the whole shell, which is what resets state between routes.

surfaces.name: games
surfaces._note: Route-driven again as of v1.20: Games left the Tools popup and is a main-window Button, so it resolves from the window root without an expand step. 'Games' also names the captured Window and the default-game ToggleButton is a UIA Button, but neither can win this step -- the Window carries no InvokePattern and a ToggleButton exposes Toggle, not Invoke, so the Type+Verb pair the resolver requires leaves exactly one match.

surfaces.name: tray-menu
surfaces.skip: Confirmed reachable, not routable. Right-clicking the tray icon (default-hidden behind Explorer's 'Show Hidden Icons' overflow) opens a real WPF ContextMenu as its own top-level Popup HWND owned by this process -- proven live via UI Automation (Popup element, pid matched ROROROblox.App) containing 8 MenuItems (Multi-Instance toggle, Streamer mode, Stop all Roblox instances, Open ROROROblox, Settings..., History..., Diagnostics..., Plugins..., Open log folder, Quit). Not converted: reaching it needs a right-click on an element inside Explorer's Shell_TrayWnd/overflow-flyout tree (a different process, and only reachable after invoking 'Show Hidden Icons'), which needs raw mouse-coordinate simulation. That is outside the route schema's verb vocabulary (invoke/select/expand/close-window) and Resolve-UiaElement's single-scope ($appRoot) resolution model. Converting this is a resolver-contract change, not a route addition.

surfaces.name: squad-launch
surfaces.skip: Confirmed via source, not converted. MainViewModel.OpenSquadLaunchAsync (MainViewModel.cs:2077-2097) shows the button opens SquadLaunchWindow.ShowDialog() -- a target-picker dialog -- and only calls SquadLaunchAsync (which launches Roblox clients) if the dialog returns true with a selected target. So the click itself is a dialog open, not a direct launch. Despite that, it stays on the deny list and skipped: deny-list membership is a compiled contract asserted by UiRoutesSchemaTests.NoRouteTargetsADeniedName, which pins both an Assert.Contains per entry and a hardcoded Assert.Equal on the list's total count. Removing 'Squad Launch' from deny therefore means deliberately editing that test, not just this route file -- outside this task's scope to do unilaterally.

surfaces.name: join-by-link
surfaces.skip: Confirmed reachable, not routable. MainWindow.xaml.cs:165 (OnGameComboBoxSelectionChanged) shows the trigger is selecting the '(Paste a link...)' sentinel entry in a per-account Game ComboBox (MainWindow.xaml:758-763) -- not a button. That ComboBox carries no x:Name or AutomationId and is instantiated once per saved account row, so every row's ComboBox is structurally identical and unaddressable by the route schema's Type+Name/Aid contract without an ancestor anchor, and there is no such anchor either (rows carry no distinguishing AutomationId). The only selector left would be a specific account's display name, which is live per-profile data (the route file is shared/committed) and would break on any profile with a different account list or zero accounts (the same class of gap already documented for surface 02).
